nodes.label: work_patterns Model (designed, not built)
nodes.rationale: The attendance calendar hardcodes Mon-Fri=8h, Sat=4h, Sun=rest inside src/app/(pages)/attendance/page.tsx. That is wrong for anyone who rests on a day other than Sunday, works six days, or works shifts - their gauge, their 'Short day' flag and the whole month summary are wrong. The replacement resolves the pattern role -> location -> company -> default.

nodes.label: Hardcoded Calendar Hours (Mon-Fri 8h / Sat 4h / Sun rest)
Deploy App Before firestore.rules
nodes.rationale: Rules resolve every capability from Firebase Auth custom claims, and only authClaims.ts mints them. A session that has not yet passed through the new AuthProvider carries a token with no capability claims, so tightened rules deny it. Ship the app, let people load it, then push the rules.

nodes.label: CLAIMED_CAPABILITIES / claims() Lockstep
nodes.rationale: A claim the rules read but nobody mints reads as false, which is how rule helpers ended up stubbed to isAuth() for months and made every signed-in employee a system admin.

nodes.label: AuthProvider onAuthStateChanged Gate
nodes.rationale: _hasHydrated on the auth store only means zustand finished reading localStorage; it says nothing about auth.currentUser. Reading Firestore too early returns permission-denied on a perfectly valid session, so AuthProvider gates on the first onAuthStateChanged callback.

nodes.label: Firestore Rules Are Default-Deny
nodes.rationale: A new collection with no match block has every read and write silently denied; this has caused real bugs more than once.

nodes.label: firestore.rules Deploy Targets ((default) and test only)
nodes.rationale: The southernlanka database is not a deploy target, so firestore.southernlanka.rules never ships from this repo - do not assume a new collection is readable there.

nodes.label: i18n Parity Enforced by TKey
nodes.rationale: Every user-facing string needs en + si + ta entries in TRANSLATIONS; the three blocks must hold the same keys in the same order or TKey breaks the build.

nodes.label: --success / --primary / --brand Resolve to One Azure
nodes.rationale: Hue alone cannot distinguish states in this palette - use shape, weight or text instead.

nodes.label: No Overtime Pay in Attendance UI
nodes.rationale: Labelling extra hours 'Overtime' implies an entitlement that does not exist. The calendar says 'Extra hours'; payroll's PH/Poya multipliers are a separate, genuinely paid concept.

nodes.label: Approval Routing Rules (approvalRouting.ts)
nodes.rationale: A routing rule that can return false for EVERY viewer leaves sessions pending forever and nothing else surfaces them. Shift-place routing did exactly that: a place tagged 'shift' routed only to the employee's assigned supervisor and overrode the place's own supervisor_epfs, so a location supervisor of that place saw nothing to approve. Rules were extracted into a pure, unit-tested module and real data is checked by replaying them with the Admin SDK.

nodes.label: Tenancy Model (one deployment, many domains)
nodes.rationale: There is no tenant list in the codebase - tenants live in their own Firestore database and are edited at /platform, so features are switched per tenant through TenantFeatures rather than by checking tenant.id at a call site.

nodes.label: src/lib/tenants.ts Purity Constraint
nodes.rationale: It takes the tenant list as an argument and must never import firebase, so both browser and server can use the same host-matching logic.

nodes.label: tenantRegistry: awaitTenants vs tenantsSync
nodes.rationale: tenantsSync() never blocks and is what adminDbFor uses; awaitTenants() blocks and is what the root layout uses.

nodes.label: window.__TENANT__ Injection Ordering
nodes.rationale: The root layout is force-dynamic and resolves the host before any bundle runs; that ordering is load-bearing - it is why module-scope reads like `const F = tenant.features` still work.

nodes.label: tenants.snapshot.json Cold-Start Failsafe
nodes.rationale: Machine-written by npm run tenants:snapshot and never hand-edited; it is the cold-start failsafe and the only list Edge middleware can read.

nodes.label: TenantFeatures Flags
nodes.rationale: One flag per page on top of the cross-cutting ones, so a page inside a subsystem needs both (e.g. /payroll-runs needs payroll AND payrollRuns).

nodes.label: MODULE_ROUTES Route-to-Flag Map
nodes.rationale: The app shell refuses to render an off-module route, so a new page needs a flag, a MODULE_ROUTES entry and its sidebar gate - hiding a nav row is never on its own enough to keep anyone out of a page.

nodes.label: System Admin (is_system_admin)
nodes.rationale: A capability on a role in ONE tenant's roles collection: full access to that system, ending at that system's border. Most administrators are this and should stay this.

nodes.label: Super Admin (isSuperAdminUser)
nodes.rationale: Granted either by a role capability or the per-user AppUser flag; both resolve through the single definition isSuperAdminUser(). superAdminSync mirrors the account into every tenant database, which is what makes 'every system' true - scope is still 'every system this account exists in', the mirror rather than a standing authority over the deployment.

nodes.label: Platform Admin (platform_admins registry)
nodes.rationale: The only cross-tenant authority in the app, granted by email in the tenants registry database and verified server-side. The platform_admin custom claim is a presentation hint and never an authority.

nodes.label: verifyPlatformCaller Server-Side Check
nodes.rationale: A role can never grant Platform Admin: roles are edited inside a tenant, so if ticking a box in one organisation could confer platform access, anyone who can edit roles there would own every other organisation in the deployment. Widening verifyPlatformCaller to consult a role, capability, claim or users doc breaks this.

nodes.label: Verification Commands (tsc, node:test, next build --webpack)
nodes.rationale: Plain `next build` FAILS in this repo - the --webpack flag is required. Only one build can run at a time; retry if it reports a lock.
